title: Scope
concept: Variables declared inside a block {} exist only within that block — this is called scope.
why: Scope prevents variables from leaking into places they don't belong, reducing bugs and making code easier to reason about.
tips: Variables exist only within the `{ }` where they're declared
Parameters exist only within their function
You can nest scopes — inner can see outer, but outer can't see inner
Use blocks to isolate temporary variables and keep code clean
common_mistakes: Trying to use a variable outside its scope — compiler will catch this
Declaring the same variable name twice in the SAME scope (without shadowing)
Assuming variables persist after their block ends
